svg.text: FinSight AI, Phase 1: user journey - uploading a document
Strict upload form, tenant and duplicate gates, virus scan, then an idempotent Step Functions ingestion pipeline that commits in one transaction.
Standard setup shown; pilot uses 1 cell. Grounded in phase1_mvp_plan.md (D3, D4, D5, D6) and the upload flow in finsight_mvp_hld.svg.
Identity, routing, store
Compute
Write / tenant create
Read / answer
Gate that refuses
Config, rules, evidence
A. Upload form and input gate
The upload form is strict. Validation happens before any bytes are stored.
Upload form fields
company_id (from token, never from body), document_category (from documents.categories).
period (YYYY-QX or YYYY-MM), status (draft|final), upload_type (new|update).
replaces_document_id (required when update), file picker: PDF, scanned PDF, Excel, CSV, DOCX.
Allowed extensions and size limits enforced; metadata validated against config/permissions.yaml.
Input gate (rejects early)
File type and size check, category exists, role may access that category and action.
Unknown category or unknown role stops the request; it never defaults.
No question text, chunk text, PII or answer content in logs.
B. Onboarding and duplicate gates
The tenancy and version rules are enforced before storage.
Onboarding gate
The company partition must exist, else the upload is refused with a clear 'partition missing' error.
No S3 object is saved and no job is queued while the partition is missing.
Duplicate check
Same file hash, or same company/category/period/name, is detected.
The API suggests an update instead of silently overwriting.
The upload form surfaces the warning and lets the user confirm.
Versioning and delta tracking (D5)
Every update creates a new version; answers cite the latest final version.
Pages and chunks are hashed; stable chunk ids; only changed chunks are embedded.
Old versions kept for version_retention_days (365); delete is soft for deleted_retention_days (30).
Delta tracking has both true and false paths; both are implemented and tested.
C. Pre-signed upload, virus scan, then queue
Bytes go to S3 first; the job is queued only after the scan passes.
Pre-signed S3 upload link
Returns a short-lived, single-file pre-signed link.
Object lands under <company_id>/<document_id>/<version>/, KMS encrypted.
One bucket per environment and region, one folder per company.
Virus scan at upload
Runs after the file lands in S3, before any queue entry.
Rejects the upload before the job is queued if the scan fails.
No job is ever queued for an infected or rejected file.
Enqueue (SQS + Step Functions)
One queue per cell, with a per-company cap on running jobs (5.21).
Failed jobs go to a retry list and raise an alert; retries are safe to repeat.
The job carries the company id; the worker rebuilds RequestContext.
D. Ingestion pipeline (Step Functions, one worker per step)
Read, delta, chunk, embed, save and cascade are separate handlers. Every step is safe to repeat.
4a Detect type and route pages
Table and layout heavy pages go to the table reader; text pages to the cheap reader.
Scanned pages route to the scan reader (pilot Tesseract, standard Textract; config-selected).
Both routed and non-routed paths are implemented and tested.
4b Delta check (updates only)
Hash raw pages and chunk ids first; skip unchanged pages (no full read).
Duplicate files are flagged rather than silently re-ingested.
Embed only new or changed chunks.
4c Extract text and tables
pdfplumber for born-digital PDFs; scan reader is Tesseract in pilot, Textract in standard; parsers for Excel, CSV, DOCX.
Each extracted number carries a confidence score; low confidence flags needs_review, never guessed.
Page numbers and tables are preserved for citations.
4d Tag metadata
Company, period, category, currency, units attached.
Missing metadata flags needs_review rather than being guessed.
Status (draft/final) and upload type are validated at the API.
4e Chunk by structure
Headings and paragraphs; tables are never split.
Parent-child chunks with stable chunk ids.
Context header plus child chunk (size from config).
4f Embed chunks
Gemini embeddings behind the port (D9), retry logic from config.
Embeddings run in batches; failures retry, then wait in the retry list.
Embedding model version is stored for reprocessing.
E. Transactional save, cascade and status
Aurora is the source of truth. Commit, then ready.
4g Save in one transaction
Chunks, vectors (pgvector), extracted numbers, version and job status commit together.
Lock 1 places rows in one partition; lock 2 stops any other read returning them.
Job is marked done only after the commit.
4h Cascade (updates only)
Recompute metrics, clear cached answers, mark dependents stale, flag related documents.
Other documents in the same company/period are flagged 'may be affected', never edited automatically.
The stamp moves in the same transaction, so old cache keys become unaddressable.
Cache invalidation
Upload, update or a deletion clears the answers that depend on the old stamp.
Answer cache key includes company, role, scope, question hash and the document stamp.
Cache reads re-check company and role before returning.
Status reporting
Status endpoint: Aurora is the truth; progress and queue place come from the DynamoDB rebuildable view.
Returns progress, queue place and errors for a job or document.
F. Delete, reprocess and protections
Every update creates a new version. Delete is soft first, hard later.
Delete (soft then purge)
Soft delete for deleted_retention_days (30), then purge chunks, vectors and metrics.
Answer cache cleared on delete; the audit entry stays.
Idempotent: repeated delete requests do no harm.
Reprocess (rolling)
Rolling reprocess after a chunking or embedding change, a few companies at a time.
Lower priority than live questions; safe to repeat without duplicate chunks.
No duplicate chunks because chunk ids are stable.
Protections that stay on
company_id on every repository, search, cache, queue and storage call.
Output gate is never disabled; metering and audit log always on.
All readers are first class; pilot flags toggle, they never delete code paths.
